external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A shopper who browses the storefront and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party card processor that settles payments and sends payment webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run through which shoppers browse and place orders; it receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.notes: It is the only thing exposed to the internet. Shopper accounts use email and password with a session cookie; MFA has not been rolled out.
processes.technology: Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that receives orders, reads and writes the orders database, and writes completed-order receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four data.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)
data_stores.notes: The order service uses a single application account with full read/write access. Its password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders, including which order was written and that the order service wrote it.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

data_flows.name: browse and place orders
data_flows.description: Shopper browsing and order-submission interactions with the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API
data_flows.authentication: email and password; session cookie; MFA not rolled out

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

data_flows.name: read and write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four data in the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for every completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_flows.authentication: the order service's own service account

data_flows.name: paid webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor sends a webhook to the storefront API after settling a payment to report that the order is paid.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: Authentication is uncertain: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The internet-facing zone containing the storefront API.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: It is the only thing we expose to the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: shoppers
trust_boundaries.description: The zone containing shoppers outside the storefront system.

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The internal network containing the order service and its databases.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: third party
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the third-party card processor.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is described as a storefront API through which shoppers browse and place orders.

assumptions.assumption: The order service presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: The service is reached through gRPC, which is an RPC interface rather than a web application interface.
It contains shopper addresses and card-last-four data, whose disclosure harms people or the business.

assumptions.assumption: The internet is a network trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The text distinguishes the internet-facing location from the internal core network.

assumptions.assumption: The shoppers zone is a tenant trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: Shoppers are external human users outside the system's control.

assumptions.assumption: The core network is a network trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The text identifies the core network as an internal network location.

assumptions.assumption: The third party zone is a tenant trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The card processor is explicitly described as a third party outside the system's control.
